headline: NanoEuler: GPT-2 scale LLM built from scratch in C/CUDA
summary: A developer built a GPT-2-style LLM from the ground up using C/CUDA, bypassing popular ML frameworks like PyTorch for a complete, educational project.
details: A developer has created NanoEuler, a GPT-2-scale language model built entirely from scratch using C and CUDA. This project deliberately avoids popular machine learning frameworks like PyTorch and autograd, with all forward and backward passes written and verified by hand.

The training pipeline includes a custom byte-level BPE tokenizer, pretraining on a mix of books and web data, and supervised fine-tuning into a chat model. The project aims to provide a complete and understandable training pipeline, serving as a research and educational artifact.

NanoEuler runs on CPU for a small showcase model and features a full from-scratch CUDA engine for larger models. A ~116M-parameter model can be trained on a single RTX 4070 GPU, utilizing hand-written FlashAttention and validated gradients against a CPU reference.

The project's name, NanoEuler, is a nod to Leonhard Euler and the forward-Euler method for numerical integration. This concept is applied to deep residual networks, where each layer integrates the hidden state forward by one Euler step, viewing a ResNet as a discretized ODE.

While the ~116M model produces fluent-looking English, it has limited real-world knowledge, similar to GPT-2-small. The fine-tuned chat model demonstrates the pipeline's effectiveness but is not a capable assistant, highlighting the need for vastly more parameters, data, and compute for truly useful conversational AI.

Forget PyTorch. This developer built a GPT-2 scale LLM entirely from scratch in C/CUDA, including hand-written backprop and FlashAttention.

A developer has created NanoEuler, a GPT-2-scale language model built entirely from scratch using C and CUDA. This project deliberately avoids popular machine learning frameworks like PyTorch and autograd, with all forward and backward passes written and verified by hand.

The training pipeline includes a custom byte-level BPE tokenizer, pretraining on a mix of books and web data, and supervised fine-tuning into a chat model. The project aims to provide a complete and understandable training pipeline, serving as a research and educational artifact.

NanoEuler runs on CPU for a small showcase model and features a full from-scratch CUDA engine for larger models. A ~116M-parameter model can be trained on a single RTX 4070 GPU, utilizing hand-written FlashAttention and validated gradients against a CPU reference.

The project's name, NanoEuler, is a nod to Leonhard Euler and the forward-Euler method for numerical integration. This concept is applied to deep residual networks, where each layer integrates the hidden state forward by one Euler step, viewing a ResNet as a discretized ODE.

While the ~116M model produces fluent-looking English, it has limited real-world knowledge, similar to GPT-2-small. The fine-tuned chat model demonstrates the pipeline's effectiveness but is not a capable assistant, highlighting the need for vastly more parameters, data, and compute for truly useful conversational AI.
